name: Eric D Johnston
residence: Southwest of Wheatland, Platte County (permanent home there since 1996, per his 2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
occupation: Farmer (alfalfa); retired from a career in upstream oil and gas; registered professional engineer in Wyoming and Texas, listed as inactive (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
education: Finished high school in Texas; two engineering degrees from Texas A&M University (specific degree titles not stated in the questionnaire)
military: Second lieutenant, U.S. Army (Engineers), between his two degrees; later served in the Reserves (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
prior_offices: One term as a Platte County Commissioner (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
background: In his 2024 WyoFile questionnaire, Eric D. Johnston wrote that he lived southwest of Wheatland, had made his permanent home there in 1996 after working overseas, is a Wyoming native, and had lived in Wyoming for more than half his life. He described himself as a third-generation Platte County resident and, when asked his age on Election Day 2024, wrote that he carried a Medicare card and was over 65.

He wrote that after starting life in Platte County he finished high school in Texas, earned two engineering degrees at Texas A&M University, and between those degrees served as a second lieutenant in the U.S. Army (Engineers), later finishing his military service in the Reserves. He said most of his professional career was in upstream oil and gas exploration and production, and that he is a registered professional engineer in Wyoming and Texas (inactive). After retirement he took over operation of his farm, raising alfalfa for cow and goat dairies. He also wrote that he served one term as a Platte County commissioner and worked to secure funding for infrastructure projects in the county and its towns.
